Azkare (Y86) / Sunrise Empire (Y00)

Region (English scoring-table region): Haless.

One-line identity: Start as a small township in Haless, give different peoples seats in parliament, and then try to turn the ideal of the “Sunrise Empire” into an institution capable of ruling a continent.

Story: very high｜Mission-tree length: very long (the local structured database shows 61 direct Y86 missions and 124 related Y00 missions; they inherit across stages and must not simply be added together)｜Mission-tree update: the local mission file was modified on 2026-07-09 and supports v1.37.5.0｜Distinctiveness: very high｜Tedium: rather high｜Early pressure: high｜Expansion capacity: very high

Identity and pre-1444 history

The current Chinese localisation renders Azkare (Y86) as 阿兹卡雷. In 1444 it is already a township in Thidinkai, Haless, not an old name for the “Sunrise Empire”. The starting-history script sets it up as a republic dominated by Sikai humans and accepting Sunrise Elves, with a historical friendship with Y59. The English offline Wiki adds that it was one of the Kai Townships and one of the few nations in Haless ever ruled by an elf, without claiming that it was the only one. The religion listed by the Wiki differs from the current local starting script; this article does not rewrite the current game setup on that basis.

The ruler Hiderion Tonanzuir was not born a hereditary monarch. Current mission text says that he was born to an elven peasant family in Azkare, served the Prakuong family for years, and earned adoption and lordship through ability; the country-history script dates his accession to 1438. The revised township history on the offline Wiki further records that in 1441 he defeated the combined armies of two neighbouring townships with newly formed cavalry; that is Wiki-reported pre-start history, not a battle the mission tree necessarily requires the player to replay. His peasant origins and his dual identity as an elven ruler are the starting point of the story: he wants ordinary Sikai people to enter the court, but must answer a harder question—how can an elf-led ideal gain the genuine consent of those it rules?

National story: from township to Sunrise

The early missions have Azkare visit, ally with, or conquer neighbouring townships to gain connections, land, and military strength; Hiderion’s old friends, new allies, and local lords are not merely “map-painting targets”. The country gradually builds fortifications, industry, and armies, turning negotiations between townships into a political mechanism representing different cultures. After completing “Guardian of the Townships”, the dedicated parliament’s representation, acceptance, and autonomy management begin to matter. Equal treatment does not arrive automatically with every conquest: whether a culture is represented directly affects which later missions can proceed.

The middle section reaches beyond Thidinkai. Missions frame wars in Xia, the south, the coast, and other parts of Haless as protection, liberation, and the reorganisation of order; at the same time, they require a new capital, Sunharbour, and transport networks. “Dawn of a New Era” is not an ordinary “conquer land and instantly transform” button: the mission requires political and construction conditions, requires the parliament to have no unrepresented culture, and then fires a dedicated event that changes Y86 into the Sunrise Empire (Y00), establishes the Sunrise Court reform, and continues the imperial missions. The generic “Form the Sunrise Empire” decision explicitly excludes Y86; conflating the two formation routes misses the core of this country’s story.

After the Empire forms, the missions continue to develop regional representation, north–south transport, ports, and a mixed military system, bringing Haless’s peoples into a political community far larger than Azkare’s homeland. Sikai cavalry, Phoenix-Legion-inspired lancers, Xia martial arts, and Nephrite Dwarf artillery present an image of a military that is unified without being completely homogenised. These wars and this Empire are not established facts of 1444; they are possible futures created by the mission tree.

Why it plays differently

  1. Parliamentary representation is not decoration. Culture groups have seats and representation, and changing representation costs resources and time; key missions require specific cultures to be represented or require an entire culture group to have no one excluded. The faster you expand, the more political integration work you create.
  2. The ruler and the institution pull against each other. Hiderion’s personal prestige can open the way, but the country must turn the ideal into representation, republican tradition, and local autonomy. Maintaining an “elven arbiter” position while claiming political equality creates a persistent tension worth engaging with.
  3. The long campaign has a clear turning point. The township phase is about survival and uniting the Sikai; the middle phase prepares the new state with a capital and representation; only after forming Y00 does the campaign enter wider Halessi integration. The 61 direct Y86 missions and 124 related Y00 missions come from the same mission file and inherit by stage; they are not an independent total.
  4. There is a genuine divergence. When Hiderion dies, if the townships have already been united and a Sikai successor is chosen, an event can redirect the campaign to Thangoya (Z62) and exchange the missions. This is an optional branch away from the Sunrise route, not a required step from Y86 to Y00.

History, ideals, and controversy

The Hiderion page in the English offline Wiki calls the “Sunrise Empire” a theoretical empire proposed by Hiderion, rather than a state already built in the setting’s history. The existing Chinese research also discusses criticisms of the ideal: too few Sunrise Elves to staff a continent-wide bureaucracy; a lack of shared political tradition across Haless; and limits on religions and cultures regarded as “foreign”. This batch did not read a Sunrise Empire main page, and the three Wiki pages actually read here do not independently verify those detailed criticisms. The Wiki’s unrealised setting history and the player-completable game route must therefore both be retained; neither replaces the other.

The 2022 official Dev Diary places the multi-cultural parliament, township origins, and imperial ideal at the centre of the design; the same year’s Warlords of Haless release announcement confirms that this mission line launched at that time. They explain the design lineage; current conditions remain governed by the local script. A 2022 test branch and a 2023 player post both mention a vulnerable opening, pressure from stronger neighbours, and the cost of managing the parliament; those are experiences from specific periods and cannot serve as guarantees of 2026 mechanics.

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 92/100｜Autocracy 55/100｜Magic↔Artifice 50/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 14/100)｜Pluralism 90/100. This is a route aimed at conquest and integration, yet it requires multi-cultural representation and republican institutions; an elven leader and imperial court still make it something other than a fully egalitarian liberal republic. Magic and artifice are not the clearest gameplay axis; the centre of gravity is political representation and military unification.

The v2.1 values result is Good (77/100), with a mixed trajectory. Bringing local peoples into politics, opposing aristocratic birth monopolies, and building transport and public order are clear positive aims; but expanding the represented polity through war, placing elves in the arbiter’s role, and setting boundaries for outsiders keep dignity and restraint from reaching the maximum. The score does not penalise expansion, imperialisation, or elven identity by themselves.

This suits players who want a long narrative campaign, a weak opening, parliament and culture management, and the integration of Haless. It does not suit players who only want continuous conquest without maintaining representation, republican tradition, and construction prerequisites, nor players who expect this idealistic expedition to have no political contradictions. See the original Chinese evidence page and the English-text review receipt for detailed sources and unresolved items.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in order as the idea group is invested in; the ambition applies after all seven ideas are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed, without racial, government, or mission rewards; a new idea set after formation is not automatically stacked with the old one. Idea descriptions may look back on history or describe a future ideal; they do not automatically mean that the content had happened by 1444.

Azkare (Y86) — Azkare Ideas

Traditions: Azkare Traditions

Effect: Aggressive expansion impact: -10%; Possible advisors: +2.

Idea 1: Son of Tonan

The elf Hiderion was born an unknown peasant, his family name coming from Lord Tonan Prakuong, who took notice of his talents and informally adopted him. For two human generations he served as a valued advisor and retainer of the Azkare lords, being granted lordship for his loyal service to the township.

For a peasant to rise to become the most powerful man in the land serves as an inspiration to the masses of Azkare, who work tirelessly in hopes of replicating his meteoric rise to power.

Effect: Advisor cost: -15%.

Idea 2: Citadel of the Dawn

At the center of Azkare is the Citadel of the Dawn, a fortress built by the Phoenix Empire to overlook the trade routes of the upper Telebei as it passes through the area. The city was built around this bastion, which has been maintained as the palace of our lords, its soaring walls still protecting Azkare and allowing a thriving market to be established just outside of it.

Effect: Fort defense: +15%; Global trade power: +5%.

Idea 3: Khanvuphaim

Khanvuphaim is a unique fabric only found in Azkare, woven from feathers by master artisans using an art that has been passed down for generations. Its softness and weightlessness make it a highly prized commodity in Thidinkai and beyond.

Effect: Production efficiency: +10%.

Idea 4: Shining Lancers

The sun elves that manned the citadel of Azkare utilized a style of cavalry far different from the usual in these lands, cladding their steeds in thick armor and wielding long steel lances. The horsemen of the Phoenix Empire survive in Haless in the form of the Shining Lancers of Azkare, fully armored and decorated with Khanvuphaim garments, acting as our elite cavalry units.

Effect: Cavalry combat ability: +10%.

Idea 5: Nakhriban

Being on the border of the Xianjie, we receive many exiles from the mysterious land to our city. They reside in the Nakhriban, and earn a living by teaching our people their arts, greatly improving the quality of our armed forces.

Effect: Infantry combat ability: +10%.

Idea 6: School of the Phoenix

As the Nakhriban grows, more and more of our people learn their formerly secret arts. The most ardent and adept students are found amongst the elves of the city, who have used their long lives to develop an entirely new school, the School of the Phoenix, to be taught to every member of our armies.

By combining the martial prowess of the Xianjie monks with the discipline of the elves, our brave soldiers have become a force to be reckoned with, unwavering in their demeanor and relentless in their assault.

Effect: Discipline: +5%; Shock damage: +5%.

Idea 7: Hiderion’s Ambition

Scattered throughout the lands of Haless lie those elves left behind by the cataclysmic fall of the Phoenix Empire. Hunted out of vengeance and distrusted by most, they scrape by as best they can, living in squalor for centuries until they finally pass from this world. For most this seems a fitting punishment for the invaders and oppressors of this land, though others see a path for redemption. The great lord Hiderion ruled over his human subjects not as a tyrant but as their righteous guardian, a true servant of the people and a paragon of the ideals set by Jaerel.

For the elves of Haless to thrive in this land, they must do so as equals of those that have called this land home for millennia, united in harmony under an serene empire, built on the virtues Hiderion lived by. We must not rule Haless as conquerors, nor as her "saviors". We must rule as her guardians, protectors of the peace and sentinels against those that would seek to exploit her.

Effect: Province warscore cost: -15%.

Ambition: Azkare Ambition

Effect: Development cost: -10%.

Sunrise Empire (Y00) — Sunrise Empire Ideas

Traditions: Sunrise Empire Traditions

Effect: Yearly corruption: -0.15; Diplomatic reputation: +100% (inherited display; unit conversion unverified; the current script value is diplomatic_reputation = 1).

Idea 1: First Unifier of Haless

While Harimar managed to conquer the Rahenraj and Yanshen, he and his descendants never had the means nor desire to conquer the rest of Haless proper. Jaher, however, did not have those limitations. By the time of Jaher's death in 1127, the Phoenix Empire stretched from Bulwar to Tianlou to Arawkelin, and even the stalwart kingdoms of the Sikai were in talks of joining the empire as a peaceful partner.

With the resurgence of the Phoenix Empire in Haless, it is by right that Haless be united under a single benevolent entity once again.

Effect: Core-creation cost: -25%.

Idea 2: Erlak-szel-Dazal

Meaning 'noblesse oblige' or 'nobility obliges', this phrase hearkens back to the sun elven attitudes as benevolent and impartial rulers of the land. Because of their duty to rule and to protect, the sun elven people must be held to higher accountabilities and expectations. They must be a good force in the world; kind and generous, patient with even those that disobey, and ultimately, be the embodiment of Surael in the world.

Effect: Stability cost modifier: -10%; National unrest: -1.

Idea 3: Jaerelic Legions

Formed by an elite cadre of Transmutative Path monks and Sikai warriors, the Jaerelic Legions became the modern version of Jaher's Phoenix Legions with one core difference: they accepted and heavily utilized non-elves. While this style was also adopted by the Jaddari, the legions of the Sunrise Empire focused on the collective values of the Halessi peoples and incorporated the ritualistic gestures of the Transmutative Path in their drilling techniques, making them a fierce opponent in the field.

Their most famous technique was the 'Burning Dragon Technique', which was essentially a fire-and-advance tactic done at an incredibly fast pace, allowing an entire regiment to continuously fire on the enemy immediately prior to entering into melee range.

Effect: Infantry fire: +15%.

Idea 4: Equals Beneath the Rising Sun

Unlike his father, who dreamed only of conquest, and his sister, who dreamed of elven supremacy, Jaerel dreamed of a world united as one - regardless of race, creed or belief, which he espoused to a point in making the love of his life, the harimari princess Tataka, his primary wife. Unfortunately, Jaerel's stance was only seen as a failure to choose a side, which saw many of his allies abandon him.

Times have changed, however, and as the world is led by the scions of Anbennar, a realm created to bring peace and equality, perhaps Haless is now ready to see that All Are Equals Beneath the Rising Sun.

Effect: Heathen tolerance: +2; Heretic tolerance: +2.

Idea 5: Rezan Zimhar

Rezan Zimhar. The Alliance of the Sun. Found and translated by scholars in the 19th century from a lost part of Jaerel's will, the Rezan Zimhar was a plan to essentially federalize the disparate and diverse cultures and religions of Haless into a united state which granted them great amounts of autonomy and privileges, all under an impartial sun elven central court. Assumed to be greatly inspired by events surrounding the collapse of Jaerel's empire-building efforts, he had hoped to present this proposal at Sarisung shortly before he was assassinated.

Now that the Sunrise Empire shines ones again, perhaps Jaerel's ambition can now be realized.

Effect: Governing capacity modifier: +20%.

Idea 6: Monks of the Weaving Palm

The sun elves brought with them arcane magic, a form of magic that was mastered through study and learning. Before that, most magic-users in Haless either utilized chi (their spiritual energy) or were outcasts studying rough forms of arcane, druidic, or other magics in the fringes of Halessi society.

The Monks of the Weaving Palm were a collection of sun elven magi, high philosophers and Transmutative Path monks who apparently spent a hundred days and nights debating on the nature of spirits and magic in the High Temple of Tianlou.

There, they developed a concept of magic that was described as 'the weave', something that one must connect with on a spiritual basis to master, not just through study. While the concept of 'the weave' never reached wide-spread popularity, the Monks of the Weaving Palm proved incredibly deadly in battle, evoking arcane spells through movements and gestures akin to chi and cultivation practices, using nothing but their internal energies - the arcane 'weave' in the air - rather than spell reagents and components.

Effect: Shock damage: +10%.

Idea 7: We All Lift Together

A common saying within the Sunrise Empire, possibly originating from ancient Yan proverbs, "We All Lift Together" was a slogan used during the industrialization initiatives of the Age of Artificery when many factories, funded by artificers and magnates, were created across Haless. It is said that the unity of the Sunrise Empire saw that every man, woman and child, regardless of race, had a role in lifting up the empire - or in a factory's case, worked as one in an assembly line.

Effect: Production efficiency: +20%.

Ambition: Sunrise Empire Ambition

Effect: Administrative efficiency: +5%.
